title: Production processes - 123 school
heading: Production processes
intro: You learn these terms and calculations by practising. Only use BINAS when the question names a BINAS table.

questions.question: What is a production chain?

answers.a: a series of steps from raw material via intermediate products to end product
answers.b: a list of all hazardous substances
answers.d: the place where a factory stands

questions.question: What do the arrows in a block diagram show?
How do you show a recycled substance in a block diagram?

answers.b: an arrow to the last block
answers.c: a dotted line to the outside
answers.d: an arrow back to an earlier block

questions.question: What is the correct order of a production chain for a plastic bag?

answers.b: crude oil → naphtha → ethene → polyethylene → bag

questions.question: Which process turns ethene into the polymer polyethylene?
Why does a factory mix starting substances in the right mass ratio?

answers.c: otherwise a substance is left over and that is a waste
answers.d: otherwise a different salt always forms

questions.question: What is an excess?

answers.a: a starting substance of which some is left after the reaction
answers.b: a starting substance that has been used up completely
answers.c: a substance that speeds up the reaction

questions.question: What is the mass ratio hydrogen : oxygen : water for 2 H<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> → 2 H<sub>2</sub>O?
How many grams of oxygen are needed for 8.0 g of hydrogen? (mass ratio 4.0 : 32.0 : 36.0)
You let 8.0 g of hydrogen react with 32.0 g of oxygen (mass ratio 4.0 : 32.0 : 36.0). Which substance is in excess?
For C + O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> the mass ratio is 12.0 : 32.0 : 44.0. How many grams of CO<sub>2</sub> are formed from 6.0 g of carbon?
Methane burns according to CH<sub>4</sub> + 2 O<sub>2</sub> → CO<sub>2</sub> + 2 H<sub>2</sub>O. What is the mass ratio methane : oxygen?
How many grams of CO<sub>2</sub> are formed from 32.0 g of methane in complete combustion? (mass ratio methane : CO<sub>2</sub> = 16.0 : 44.0)
For ammonia, N<sub>2</sub> + 3 H<sub>2</sub> → 2 NH<sub>3</sub> with mass ratio 28.0 : 6.0 : 34.0. You have 14.0 g of nitrogen and 6.0 g of hydrogen. Which substance is in excess?
From which substance does industry get the nitrogen for ammonia?
Why does a factory feed substances that have not reacted back into the process?

answers.d: so the product becomes more poisonous

questions.question: An ore sample of 200 g contains 140 g of iron oxide. What is the mass percentage of iron oxide?
Wine of 750 mL contains 12 volume percent alcohol. How many mL of alcohol is that?
Air contains 21 volume percent oxygen. How many litres of oxygen are in 50 L of air?
From 319.2 g of iron oxide, 223.2 g of iron is formed. How many grams of iron are formed from 159.6 g of iron oxide?
What is an intermediate product?

answers.a: the end product the customer buys
answers.c: a substance that is made in the chain and then used again

questions.question: What is a raw material?

answers.a: a substance that is formed at the end of the process
answers.b: a substance from nature with which a production process starts
answers.c: a substance that only consists of metals
